vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: privacy-policy
Version: 2.2.0

The skill is a legitimate utility for generating privacy policy templates (GDPR, CCPA, etc.). The core logic in scripts/privacy.sh is a straightforward bash script that uses heredocs to output text based on user-provided arguments like company name and email. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill and included script are internally consistent with a privacy-policy generator: no credentials, no install, and the script prints policy text; however part of the script was truncated in the provided bundle so I couldn't fully verify there are no hidden network or file operations.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the actual files: SKILL.md documents commands to generate GDPR/CCPA/app/website policies and the provided scripts/privacy.sh implements a template-based policy generator that accepts company/email/website parameters. There are no unrelated credentials or binaries requested.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for generating privacy policies and is low-risk based on the visible files — it templates policy text to stdout and takes company/email/website arguments. Before installing or running it in production, review the full scripts/privacy.sh file (the provided snippet was truncated) for any of the following signs of unexpected behavior: network calls (curl, wget, nc, ssh, scp), remote endpoints or IP addresses, commands that read system files (~/.aws, /etc, /home/*), commands that send data (curl POST, nc, mail), eval/exec of untrusted input, or writes to system paths. Also inspect the implementation of the audit subcommand to ensure it only performs local, non-sensitive checks and does not attempt to exfiltrate data. Run the script in a sandbox with test inputs first, and remember the generated text is not legal advice — consult a lawyer before publishing a policy.
